title: Logical buffer limits through Avro's Hadoop converter
summary: The original converter factory must preserve the physical capacity and expose exactly the BytesWritable logical prefix.

change.description: The original converter factory must preserve the physical capacity and expose exactly the BytesWritable logical prefix.

verdictLabel: Native 3/10 at original scope, 10/10 across observed startup scopes, finite JVM 10/10
notes: The November 22 expansion proved that the actual Jackson JsonFactory initializes on both revisions for all modeled clock readings at unwind 512. At the frozen unwind of 64 the ordinary direct path still needs the cells from the character-table loop. The Hadoop reducer lookup on a fresh JobConf(false) returns one twice under a startup capture of JobConf and Credentials. The public converter factory also requires ordinary configuration and schema initialization. An explicit XML resource returned seven on the JVM, and a malformed overlay raised NumberFormatException. The current per-stage obligations are recorded in verification/domain-foundations/expansion.json.
The frozen independent observation table has 21 rows. Each property identifies its own input range. The subject JDK is Temurin 21.0.13.

With capacity five and logical length three, the parent had position/limit/capacity/remaining (0,5,5,5) and read 4 at index 3. The fix had (0,3,5,3) and threw IndexOutOfBoundsException. Both returned the prefix 1, 2, 3 with position zero. The nested converter is scored separately from the real JobConf(false) factory.

Class intake now checks the actual source and bytes selected by the subject JVM for declared dependency overlaps. Both historical closures contain 124 entries and seven differing package metadata classes. Native startup reaches Hadoop Configuration from the factory and Avro Schema from the direct route. The initial startup observations stopped at System.getenv and Runtime.availableProcessors respectively.

On the original JDK with two processors and an empty process environment, the factory observation reaches Hadoop Configuration’s use of File.getAbsoluteFile. The nested converter with two processors reaches a write by Avro Schema initialization into Accessor.jsonPropertiesAccessor. It holds a JsonProperties$1 instance after Schema initializes and is null when Accessor initializes alone. These single-class startup claims remain open.

With Schema and BytesWritable initialized together before the entry on JDK 21.0.13, two CPUs, an empty environment and the Unix root working directory, the native checker proved the fixed public nested converter over all 21 registered inputs. At selector 1 the parent leaves a one-byte array readable after its logical length is reduced to zero. The native candidate returned 0 through the original parent adapter in a fresh JVM with ambient startup. The source artifacts, typed inputs, observations and state hashes are in the workflow receipts.

The eight factory tasks in the earlier two-root scope stopped at JobConf initialization. Adding JobConf as a third root reached Collections.newSetFromMap, then the real Hadoop weak registry once the checker executed the JDK's map-backed set.

The strict checker decided all eight public factory obligations after Schema, BytesWritable, JobConf and Credentials initialized in that order on Temurin 21.0.13 with two processors, an empty environment and / as the working directory. Both original classpaths gave the same 220-class, 1,079-object state, 540f78ac686458dc4648b26cafe10fde211ffc3231f0965ce5fd67494e7cad64. The checker executed new JobConf(false), AvroDatumConverterFactory.create, conversion and the buffer observations. Bounds, prefix and first-index checks cover all 21 inputs on each revision. The separate full-length control fixes capacity and length at five.

The native parent failed both factory bounds and rejection at selector 1, a one-byte backing array with logical length zero. Two fresh JVM replays admitted that input through the original factory without early initialization. Together with the public nested converter, three original parent obligations have native counterexamples replayed on the original JVM. The seven universal native results retain their stated startup conditions.

The domain foundations pilot traced the original four-root writes, including the JsonProperties accessor installation. Fresh native proofs establish the real superclass registration and its erroneous second-use behavior. The writable shrink contract covers arbitrary bytes through length six under the recorded startup. The bytecode and field tables are in verification/domain-foundations/dependencies.

On both historical classpaths the checker qualified the 56 instructions that build distinct schema and enum reserved-name sets. The enum adds default while the schema set retains its ten names. With only Schema initialized in advance, two public BYTES constructions returned distinct schemas of the right type and RECORD raised AvroRuntimeException. The results and remaining Jackson dependency are in verification/domain-foundations/followup.json.
